source_text: Quaero enim, cur epistulae huius principium sit: Manichaeus apostolus Iesu Christi, et non sit: paracletus apostolus Iesu Christi. si autem missus a Christo paracletus Manichaeum misit, cur lego: Manichaeus apostolus Iesu Christi, et non potius: Manichaeus apostolus paracleti? si dicis ipsum esse Christum, qui est etiam spiritus sanctus, contradicis ipsi scripturae, ubi dominus ait: et alium paracletum mittam uobis. si autem ideo Christi nomen recte positum putas, non quia ipse est Christus, qui et paracletus, sed quia eiusdem sunt ambo substantiae, id est. non quia unus est, sed quia unum sunt, poterat et Paulus dicere: Paulus apostolus dei patris, quia dixit dominus: ego et pater unum sumus. nusquam hoc dicit, sed nec quisquam apostolorum patris se apostolum scribit. quid sibi ergo uult ista nouitas ? nonne uobis uidetur nescio quam redolere fallaciam ? certe si nihil interesse arbitratus est, cur non uarie in aliis epistulis apostolum Christi se nominat, in aliis paracleti? sed Christi semper audiui, quotienscumque audiui, paracleti autem nec semel. quid hoc esse causae arbitramur, nisi quia illa superbia, mater omnium haereticorum, inpulit hominem, ut non missum se ab paracleto uellet uideri, sed ita susceptum, ut ipse paracletus diceretur? sicut Iesus Christus homo non a filio dei, id est uirtute et sapientia dei. per quam facta s:mt omnia, missus est, sed ita susceptus secundum catholiram fidem, ut ipse esset dei filius, id est in illo ipso dei sapientia sanandis peccatoribus adpareret: sic se ille uoluit ab spiritu sancto, quem Christus promisit. uideri esse susceptum. ut iam cum audimus Manichaeum spiritum sanctum, intellegamus apostolum Iesu Christi, id est missum a Iesu Christo, qui eum se missurum esse promisit. singularis audacia ista et ineffabile sacrilegium!
thought_title: Why Mani calls himself apostle of Jesus Christ rather than of the Paraclete
orientation: Augustine is questioning the opening title of Mani's Fundamental Letter, where Mani names himself 'apostle of Jesus Christ' rather than 'apostle of the Paraclete.'
pass_a_gloss: I ask [then], why [the] beginning of this epistle is: Manichaeus apostle of Jesus Christ, and is not: paraclete apostle of Jesus Christ. if [but] sent by Christ [the] paraclete sent Manichaeum, why [do] I read: Manichaeus apostle of Jesus Christ, and not rather: Manichaeus apostle of [the] paraclete? if you say [that] he himself is Christ, who is also [the] holy spirit, you contradict [the] scripture itself, where [the] lord says: and another paraclete I will send to you. if [but] therefore [the] name of Christ [you] think rightly placed, not because he himself is Christ, who [is] also [the] paraclete, but because of [the] same substance are both, that is, not because one is, but because one [thing] they are, could also Paul say: Paul apostle of God [the] father, because [the] lord said: I and [the] father one [thing] we are. nowhere this he says, but nor anyone of [the] apostles [as] apostle of [the] father himself writes. what to himself therefore wants this novelty? not to you does it seem I know not what to smell of deceit? certainly if nothing [it] matters he judged, why not variously in other epistles [as] apostle of Christ himself he names, in others [as] of [the] paraclete? but Christ always I have heard, as often as I have heard, of [the] paraclete [but] not even once. what this to be of cause do we think, unless because that pride, mother of all heretics, drove [the] man, that not sent himself by [the] paraclete he wished to seem, but so received, that himself [the] paraclete he might be called? just as Jesus Christ [the] man not by [the] son of God, that is [the] power and wisdom of God, through which made are all things, was sent, but so received according to [the] catholic faith, that himself he was [the] son of God, that is in that very [one] [the] wisdom of God for healing sinners might appear: so himself he wished by [the] holy spirit, whom Christ promised, to seem to have been received, that now when we hear Manichaeum [the] holy spirit, we understand [the] apostle of Jesus Christ, that is sent by Jesus Christ, who him [that] he would send promised. singular boldness this and ineffable sacrilege!

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the Holy Spirit promised by Christ; Mani claimed to be this.
Fixed glossary term for one sent with authority; Mani claimed this title.
Fixed glossary term for underlying reality or nature; here used of the shared substance of Christ and the Paraclete.
Renders the idea of a human person being assumed or received by a divine person, as in the Incarnation; Augustine contrasts Mani's claim with Christ's.

choices.english: smell of some deceit or other
choices.why: Keeps the sensory metaphor of 'redolere' (to smell of) and the indefinite force of 'nescio quam' (some or other).

choices.term: singularis audacia ista et ineffabile sacrilegium
choices.english: Singular audacity this and unspeakable sacrilege
choices.why: Preserves the exclamatory word order and the force of 'singularis' (unparalleled) and 'ineffabile' (unspeakable).

pass_b_english: For I ask why the beginning of this letter is: Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ, and not: the Paraclete, apostle of Jesus Christ. If the Paraclete was sent by Christ and then sent Mani, why do I read: Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ, and not rather: Mani, apostle of the Paraclete? If you say that he is Christ himself, who is also the Holy Spirit, you contradict the Scripture itself, where the Lord says: and I will send you another Paraclete (John 14:16). But if you think the name of Christ is rightly placed, not because he is Christ who is also the Paraclete, but because both are of the same substance—that is, not because he is one, but because they are one—then Paul could also have said: Paul, apostle of God the Father, because the Lord said: I and the Father are one (John 10:30). Nowhere does he say this, nor does any of the apostles write that he is an apostle of the Father. What then does this novelty mean? Does it not seem to you to smell of some deceit or other? Certainly if he judged that it made no difference, why does he not vary his title in other letters, calling himself apostle of Christ in some and apostle of the Paraclete in others? But I have always heard apostle of Christ, whenever I have heard it, and apostle of the Paraclete not even once. What do we suppose is the reason for this, except that that pride, the mother of all heretics, drove the man to want to appear not as one sent by the Paraclete, but as one so taken up that he himself would be called the Paraclete? Just as Jesus Christ, a man, was not sent by the Son of God—that is, by the power and wisdom of God, through which all things were made—but was so taken up according to the Catholic faith that he himself was the Son of God, that is, that in him the very wisdom of God appeared for the healing of sinners: so that man wanted to appear to have been taken up by the Holy Spirit, whom Christ promised, so that now when we hear Mani called the Holy Spirit, we understand him to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, that is, one sent by Jesus Christ, who promised that he would send him. Singular audacity this and unspeakable sacrilege!

last_rejected.quote: Just as Jesus Christ, a man, was not sent by the Son of God
last_rejected.source_quote: sicut Iesus Christus homo non a filio dei
last_rejected.why: 'homo' here means 'the man Jesus Christ' (the incarnate Christ), not 'a man' as an indefinite article.
last_rejected.fix: Just as Jesus Christ the man was not sent by the Son of God
last_rejected.ruling: 'homo' without article naturally reads 'a man' in this comparative construction; 'the man' would require 'hic homo' or context demanding definiteness.

last_rejected.quote: and I will send you another Paraclete (John 14:16)
last_rejected.why: Latin says 'another Paraclete,' English omits 'another,' weakening Augustine's argument about distinction of persons.
last_rejected.fix: and I will send you another Paraclete
last_rejected.ruling: English 'another Paraclete' is present; claim misreads the text.

last_rejected.quote: nor does any of the apostles write that he is an apostle of the Father
last_rejected.source_quote: sed nec quisquam apostolorum patris se apostolum scribit
last_rejected.why: Latin reflexive 'se' means 'write himself' or 'claim to be,' not 'that he is'; agency misattributed.
last_rejected.fix: nor does any of the apostles write himself an apostle of the Father
last_rejected.ruling: 'se apostolum scribit' = 'writes himself [as] apostle'; 'that he is' conveys same meaning adequately.

last_rejected.quote: so that now when we hear Mani called the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: ut iam cum audimus Manichaeum spiritum sanctum
last_rejected.why: Latin accusative 'Manichaeum spiritum sanctum' means 'hear Mani [as] the Holy Spirit,' not 'hear Mani called the Holy Spirit'; English adds 'called' which softens the claim.
last_rejected.fix: so that now when we hear Mani the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.ruling: 'called' is reasonable rendering of accusative-plus-noun construction; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: who promised that he would send him
last_rejected.source_quote: qui eum se missurum esse promisit
last_rejected.why: Latin 'se missurum esse' is 'promised that he himself would send him,' not 'promised that he would send him'; English omits reflexive 'himself,' obscuring Christ's agency.
last_rejected.fix: who promised that he himself would send him
last_rejected.ruling: Reflexive 'se' is implicit in 'who promised'; English already has 'he' as subject. Minor emphasis only.
